paper_title: Progressive evolutions of non-fused ring electron acceptors toward efficient organic solar cells with improved photocurrent and reduced energy loss
source_file: /home/wzfeng/MySearch/PhotoRag/MD/Progressive evolutions of non-fused ring electron acceptors toward efficient organic solar cells with improved photocurrent and reduced energy loss/auto/Progressive evolutions of non-fused ring electron acceptors toward efficient organic solar cells with improved photocurrent and reduced energy loss.md

knowledge_points.content: The molecular evolution from DF-PCIC to O-PC-EH involves terminal fluorination to form HF-PCIC, followed by replacing core fluorine atoms with alkoxy groups (linear O-PC-OC or branched O-PC-EH) to tune optoelectronic properties.
knowledge_points.evidence: HF-PCIC was obtained by fluorinating the end groups of DF-PCIC, and O-PC-X series NFREAs was designed and synthesized by further replacing the fluorine atoms on the core of HF-PCIC with different alkoxy groups: linear alkyl chain for O-PC-OC and branched alkyl chain for O-PC-EH.

knowledge_points.content: Intramolecular noncovalent interactions, specifically F...H and O...S, are utilized in NFREAs to lock the molecular geometry into a planar configuration, which is confirmed by DFT calculations showing small dihedral angles.
knowledge_points.evidence: all the molecules bear planar configurations with relatively small dihedral angles due to the formation of intramolecular F...H or O...S noncovalent interactions, which help lock the molecular geometry.

knowledge_points.content: The organic solar cell based on the J52:O-PC-EH blend achieved a peak power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 14.43%, with a certified value of 14.1%.
knowledge_points.evidence: the J52:O-PC-EH-based OSC achieved the best efficiency of 14.4% (certified: 14.1%) with benefits in all the three device parameters.

knowledge_points.content: Introducing electron-donating alkoxy groups onto the core of NFREAs effectively up-shifts the HOMO levels, narrowing the donor/acceptor energetic offset and reducing energy loss.
knowledge_points.evidence: After replacing the fluorine atoms in the core with alkoxy groups, the HOMO levels of O-PC-X molecules were up shifted effectively, owing to the strong electron-donating property of alkoxy chains, thus narrowing the donor/acceptor energetic offset.

knowledge_points.content: J52:O-PC-EH-based devices exhibit a low non-radiative voltage loss (ΔVnon-rad) of 0.301 V and a small energetic offset (ΔECT) of 0.090 eV, contributing to a total voltage loss of 0.679 V.
knowledge_points.evidence: device based on O-PC-EH exhibited... the lowest ΔVnon-rad of 0.301 V... ΔECT values for... J52:O-PC-EH-based devices were calculated as... 0.090 eV.

knowledge_points.content: The J52:O-PC-EH optimal device parameters include an open-circuit voltage (Voc) of 0.819 V, a short-circuit current density (Jsc) of 24.44 mA cm-2, and a fill factor (FF) of 72.2%.
knowledge_points.evidence: the OSCs based on J52:O-PC-EH achieved an optimal PCE of 14.43%... with a much higher FF of 72.2%, a Voc of 0.819 V and Jsc of 24.44 mA cm-2.

knowledge_points.content: Grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering (GIWAXS) reveals that O-PC-EH has a significantly higher crystal coherence length (CCL) of 250.06 Å in the in-plane (IP) direction compared to DF-PCIC, HF-PCIC, and O-PC-OC.
knowledge_points.evidence: The CCLs of DF-PCIC, HF-PCIC and O-PC-OC in the IP direction were in the range of 20~40 Å while O-PC-EH shown a much larger CCL of 250.06 Å.

knowledge_points.content: The J52:O-PC-EH device demonstrates superior carrier dynamics with an exciton-dissociation efficiency (Pdiss) of 96.03% and a charge-collection efficiency (Pcoll) of 81.86%.
knowledge_points.evidence: the J52:O-PC-EH-based device performed the best with Pdiss and Pcoll of 96.03% and 81.86%, respectively.

knowledge_points.content: The devices utilized a conventional structure consisting of ITO/PEDOT:PSS/active layer/PDINN/Ag, where PDINN serves as the cathode interlayer.
knowledge_points.evidence: The photovoltaic properties of the NFREAs were investigated by fabricating OSCs with the device configuration of ITO/PEDOT:PSS/ active layer/PDINN/Ag.

knowledge_points.content: Branched side chains in O-PC-EH, compared to linear chains in O-PC-OC, promote a larger proportion of face-on orientation and stronger crystallinity, leading to improved electron mobility and fill factor.
knowledge_points.evidence: O-PC-EH shows... a much stronger π-π stacking peak at qz = 1.72 Å-1... implying a large proportion of face-on orientation... the CCL of J52:O-PC-EH blend was the largest... contributing to the highest FF.

knowledge_points.content: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) images show that the J52:O-PC-EH blend forms a fiber-like interpenetrating network with appropriate phase separation, which facilitates exciton dissociation and charge transfer.
knowledge_points.evidence: When it comes to J52:O-PC-EH blend film, fiber-like domains with appropriate size could be observed, indicating the formation of interpenetrating network.

knowledge_points.content: The O-PC-X series of NFREAs exhibit red-shifted absorption with peaks centered around 820 nm, extending the external quantum efficiency (EQE) response range up to 900 nm.
knowledge_points.evidence: O-PC-X series NFREAs exhibit red-shifted absorption with absorption peaks centered at around 820 nm... devices based on O-PC-X series NFREAs showed the broadest photo-response ranging from 300 to 900 nm.
